clue.text: Letter from abroad to mother about royal shock

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes round the royal abbreviation, so it is placed about it

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign letter
R is the usual abbreviation for royal (as in RN, Royal Navy)
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A letter arriving from overseas tells Mum some startling royal news.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional jolt, a sense close to a nasty shock.

clue.text: Concertina you see the stars with

explanation.surface: An accordion-style instrument doubles as a stargazing device.
explanation.definitionFit: To concertina is to collapse in sections, as a telescoping tube does; the second sense is the optical instrument astronomers use.

clue.text: Husband, round in local, ordered this

definitions.text: Husband, round in local, ordered this

indicators.note: the husband and round letters sit in the middle of the rearranged pub word, so in signals insertion
ordered here means rearranged into a new sequence, so the letters of local are reshuffled

parts.note: O is round in shape, a common crossword stand-in

explanation.surface: At the pub, a husband buys a round and orders drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the letters of 'local', and 'in' puts the round and husband letters into the middle. In a pub, what you order is drink, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering a round in a local pub means asking for beer, wine and spirits, which are all intoxicating drinks.

clue.text: King at one time became a highly-strung figure

indicators.note: became signals that the letters turn into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A one-time monarch ended up a nervous, highly-strung character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' rearranges R plus the letters of AT ONE TIME. 'highly-strung' means nervy in the surface but literally means hung on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings is literally a figure strung from above, hence highly strung.

clue.text: A decadent poet encloses verse to secure patronage

indicators.note: the poet's name wraps round the letter for verse, so encloses signals insertion

parts.note: Ernest Dowson was a poet of the 1890s Decadent movement

explanation.surface: A dissolute poet slips some verse into his work to win a patron.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Dowson was an 1890s English poet of the Decadent movement. 'encloses' puts V inside DOWSON, giving DVOWSON, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: In English church law, an advowson is the right to appoint a parish's clergyman, a form of ecclesiastical patronage.

clue.text: Put up ten thousand to support butter manufacturer

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a myriad is literally ten thousand, from the Greek
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Someone stakes ten thousand to back a dairy business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' reverses MYRIAD to DAIRYM, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid traditionally churned cream on the farm, so she produced the butter.

clue.text: Old, nevertheless became king of Germany

parts.note: tho, short for though, means nevertheless

explanation.surface: An elderly man nonetheless rose to rule the Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: Otho is the old English form of Otto, the name of several German kings who became Holy Roman Emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho (Otto) was the name borne by medieval German monarchs, such as Otto the Great.

clue.text: Paintings and sculpture are up to the Corporation's level

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: painting and sculpture are the visual arts
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Galleries rise to the standard set by the city council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ARTS to STRA. 'Corporation' is not a council here but an old joke word for a paunch, TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or tier, as in a social stratum, which is a level.

clue.text: Dapper Bumppo

explanation.surface: A smart, well-dressed frontiersman.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neat in dress; Natty Bumppo is the frontier hero of Fenimore Cooper's Leatherstocking novels.

clue.text: Piano is not ostentatious

annotationWithheld.why: Piano is not ostentatious (4) for WOOD: no parse found that gives WOOD from these words, and a search of the exact clue gave nothing

clue.text: Look at the number without transport in Switzerland

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside or beyond, so the number stands just past the transport

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a car is a means of transport
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Admire the figures, minus any cars, in a Swiss setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so NO stands beyond CAR. Locarno is a lakeside town in southern Switzerland, known for the 1925 treaties.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno is a resort town in the canton of Ticino, so it lies within the Swiss border.

clue.text: Be left in their form

indicators.note: form is read as a verb, to shape, so the letters are moulded into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A request to be left in whatever shape they prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' asks for the letters of IN THEIR to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into property under a will is to be bequeathed it, that is, to receive a legacy.

clue.text: Rugby terms familiar to Slogger Williams

definitions.text: Rugby terms familiar to Slogger Williams

parts.words: Rugby terms familiar to Slogger Williams
parts.note: Rugby is the public school, terms are school terms, and Slogger Williams is the bully Tom fights in Thomas Hughes's novel of Rugby school life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby terms' suggests the sport's vocabulary, but Rugby is the English boarding school. Slogger Williams is a character in Tom Brown's Schooldays, set there.
explanation.definitionFit: Slogger Williams's terms at Rugby school were his years of pupilhood, his time as a schoolboy.

clue.text: Shore is tarry

explanation.surface: The beach is sticky with tar.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up is to prop, and a stay is a prop or support; to tarry is to linger or remain.

clue.text: Tethers donkey, having to puff all the time

parts.note: chains are things that tether
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a donkey while puffing away constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is an old British slang word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain-smoke is to light each cigarette from the last, smoking without a break.

clue.text: Boring instruction to an engineer?

parts.note: read as an order to a mechanic it means lubricate the machine thoroughly; boring means drilling, for a drilled shaft yielding petroleum

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull', but it means drilling; the phrase also reads as advice to an engineer to lubricate well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a shaft drilled into the ground to extract crude, and also an order to lubricate thoroughly.

clue.text: Masons intended, they say, to get temporary occupation

parts.note: Freemasons meet in a lodge, the name for a branch of the order

indicators.note: they say signals that the next word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Freemasons planned, so the story goes, to take over a building for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns MEANT into its sound-alike MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is a foothold or position seized and held for a time, as by troops in enemy ground.

clue.text: Has made Dicky embarrassed

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or unsound, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky has been made to blush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the British slang for shaky or faulty, signalling a rearrangement of HAS MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ashamed is feeling guilt or mortification, much like being embarrassed.

clue.text: Pay girl's commission

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, here with the possessive
a charge is a task entrusted to someone, a commission

explanation.surface: A young woman is paid her commission.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a debt is to settle it in full, so to pay it off.

clue.text: Once got subpoenaed in a state

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so once
to be cited is to be summoned to court, as by a subpoena

explanation.surface: Someone once summonsed in one of the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests a US state, but it means agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state means being worked up or agitated.

clue.text: Rebel down under ends with a flourish

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
NZ, New Zealand, is part of the land down under

explanation.surface: An Australian rebel finishes off with a showy gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a Kentish rising in 1450. 'down under' gives NZ, New Zealand; 'ends with' places A last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a showy solo passage near the end of a concerto movement, a virtuoso musical embellishment.

clue.text: Aquatic birds circling the river and woods

indicators.note: the bird word goes round the river abbreviation, so circling signals enclosure

parts.note: divers are water birds, also called loons
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Water birds wheel above the river and the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woods' looks like trees, but it means golf clubs once made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers are golf clubs traditionally made of wood, hence called woods.

clue.text: Loss of light causes cuts in the middle of speech

indicators.note: the clipping word sits inside the central letters of speech
the middle of speech means its central pair of letters

parts.note: clips means cuts, as with shears

explanation.surface: A power cut happens halfway through someone's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of light' could be a power cut, but here it is the astronomical event; 'the middle of' takes the two central letters of 'speech'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse happens when one body blocks the sun or moon, so its brightness is cut off.

clue.text: Useless English holidaymaker in America

parts.note: a dud is something useless, here as an adjective

explanation.surface: A hopeless English tourist abroad in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In the American West, a dude is a city visitor holidaying on a dude ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage a dude was an Easterner vacationing on a Western ranch, a tourist.

clue.text: Went out about noon and had a meal

indicators.note: the word for went out goes round the noon letter

parts.note: died means went out, as a light or fire does

explanation.surface: Someone went out around midday and ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went out' looks like leaving the house, but it means expired, DIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a main meal.

clue.text: He lived long in part of New England, so healthy in retirement

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, one of the New England states
thus means so, therefore

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A man from Maine reached a great age because he stayed so fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses HALE to ELAH. ME is Maine, a New England state.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the biblical patriarch said to have reached 969 years, the oldest recorded person.

clue.text: This Roman king was a countryman

parts.note: hic is Latin for this, the word a Roman would use
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Roman monarch who was a peasant.
explanation.walkthrough: A hick is a US term for an unsophisticated rural person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hick is a rustic, a person from the backwoods, so a rural dweller.

clue.text: Setting up guns suitable for men only

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means writing the word upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: gats are guns in gangster slang

explanation.surface: Arranging firearms, a job only for men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting up' reverses GATS, gangster slang for guns, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is a male-only gathering.

clue.text: Musical girl appearing after two numbers

definitions.text: Musical girl appearing after two numbers

parts.words: Musical girl appearing after two numbers
parts.note: the 1920s musical title has a girl's name preceded by two words that look like abbreviations for number

explanation.walkthrough: The musical is No, No, Nanette (1925); each No looks like the abbreviation for number.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title heroine of the 1925 musical, her name preceded by two noes.

clue.text: Cut off by a heavy fall

parts.note: to crop is to cut off, as with hair or a tail
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone is severed from the world by a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come a cropper' is a British idiom for falling badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropper is a bad tumble, as in to come a cropper.

clue.text: Drinks for the men on board

explanation.surface: Rounds of drinks for sailors aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a swallow of liquid; draughts is also the British board game (checkers) whose pieces are called men.

clue.text: Part Wilde let Ernest cut

indicators.note: part signals that only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde allowed a role in Earnest to be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to The Importance of Being Earnest; 'Part' picks letters from WILDE LET ERNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete text is to remove or strike it out.
